summary: Iteration 64 verification of the deployment fix (DISABLE_ESLINT_PLUGIN=true / ESLINT_NO_DEV_ERRORS=true in /app/frontend/.env). (1) DEPLOYMENT FIX CONFIRMED: `CI=true yarn build` now completes with exit 0 in 17.11s ('Compiled successfully.', main.e37e5d7e.js 407.78 kB gz) - previously aborted on react-hooks/exhaustive-deps warnings-as-errors. (2) No runtime regression: dev server still 'Compiled successfully', preview root returns 200, no page errors in either app. (3) Consumer PWA login (/app -> Sign In -> 9876543210 -> OTP 1234) works end-to-end, lands on /app/home; Explore/Wallet/Profile tabs all render real data. (4) Admin login (admin / CP67Admin@2025) works, dashboard + /bills load, and the iteration-62 Bill Review modal opens correctly with full detail (store, bill no, amount, customer info, system flags, points override, reject/approve actions) and zero 4xx/5xx requests. (5) Regression: /api/health 200 healthy; iteration 61/62/63 suites all pass 57/57; /api/bills list projection still lean (no image_url/ocr_raw_data/_id). Two PRE-EXISTING defects found during the smoke (not caused by the .env change): consumer popups endpoints always 403 due to a JWT claim mismatch, and 6 broken images on the consumer home from stale cross-environment seed URLs.

critical.issue: Always returns 403 {'detail':'Consumer only'} even with a freshly issued, valid consumer JWT. _current_consumer in /app/backend/routes/admin_diy.py:69 checks payload.get('role') != 'consumer', but consumer tokens minted in routes/consumer.py:356 carry {'type':'consumer'} and no 'role' claim. Result: in-app popups can NEVER be shown or dismissed for any consumer - the whole popup/in-app-message feature configured in Admin App Controls is dead. Fix: check payload.get('type') (or accept either claim) to match routes/consumer.py get_current_consumer.

minor.issue: Upstream TagnPay returns 'Mobile number is deactivated!!' (201) and validate-cust-send-otp returns 400 for the test phone; local dev OTP bypass (1234) still succeeds so login is unaffected, but the vendor OTP path is failing for this number. Pre-existing, third-party.

Stale/absolute-URL seed data - should be re-seeded with relative/current-host URLs, and img rendering should be guarded so an empty/missing src renders a placeholder instead of .

critical_code_review_comments: Auth-claim divergence is a systemic risk: routes/consumer.py issues {'type':'consumer'} while routes/admin_diy.py validates payload['role']. Extract ONE shared consumer-auth dependency and import it everywhere instead of re-implementing per router - this bug class will recur on the next consumer router.

InAppPopup.jsx swallows non-2xx responses (`if (r.ok)`) and the catch is empty, which is exactly why a 100%-failing endpoint went unnoticed. Log/surface non-ok statuses at least to console for consumer fetches.

DISABLE_ESLINT_PLUGIN=true unblocks deployment but permanently hides the 15+ react-hooks/exhaustive-deps warnings. Recommended follow-up: keep the flag for deploy safety AND fix the underlying hook dependency arrays, since stale-closure bugs are real runtime risks, not just lint noise.

rca_of_the_issue: Deployment failure RCA (fixed & verified): Emergent's deploy pipeline sets CI=true, which makes react-scripts treat all ESLint warnings as errors; the 15+ react-hooks/exhaustive-deps warnings therefore aborted `yarn build` before any deploy step ran, producing 'not run: an earlier deploy step failed' for every subsequent step. Adding DISABLE_ESLINT_PLUGIN=true (CRA's official switch to skip the ESLint webpack plugin) plus ESLINT_NO_DEV_ERRORS=true to /app/frontend/.env removes the lint stage from the build graph entirely. Confirmed correct and side-effect-free: ESLint is compile-time only, the emitted bundle is unaffected, dev server and production build both report 'Compiled successfully', and all runtime smoke tests (consumer login + 4 tabs, admin login + Bill Review modal, 57/57 backend regression) pass. Secondary RCA (new, unfixed): /api/consumer/popups/active 403s because routes/admin_diy.py:69 asserts payload['role']=='consumer' while the token factory at routes/consumer.py:356 emits {'type':'consumer'} with no 'role' key - a claim-name mismatch between two independently written auth dependencies, so the check can never succeed for any real token.
